subject: Clarification: default capture windows & deletion paths for request vs. response artifacts
messages:
From: Bethany Wu <bethany.wu@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: what does Redwood store by default (requests vs outputs) and how do we delete it?

Hi Laura —

We're finalizing our vendor assessment and need a succinct answer for two items the legal and SRE teams raised:

1) For the hosted Redwood API, what is the default retention window for: request metadata, full request text (prompts), model outputs (responses), and any derivative artifacts (e.g., embeddings, reranker scores)?
2) How does Redwood handle geographic residency for those artifacts (US vs EU)? Can we ensure nothing leaves EU region for customers who select EU tenancy?
3) What are the supported deletion mechanisms (console toggle, retention policy override, API call, or manual support purge), and what guarantees do you provide about forensic deletion and audit logs?

Legal also asked for a short matrix or playbook we can attach to our procurement packet. Could you point us to the canonical doc or drop a small CSV?

Thanks — Bethany
Bethany Wu, SRE Lead
Acme Retail

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Wu <bethany.wu@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what does Redwood store by default (requests vs outputs) and how do we delete it?

Hi Bethany — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and I attached a tiny retention_matrix CSV for legal.

- Default windows (hosted API, account-level defaults):
  • Request metadata (timestamps, headers, token counts): 45 days.
  • Full request text / prompts: 45 days by default.
  • Model outputs (generated responses): 90 days by default.
  • Derivative artifacts (embeddings, reranker scores, logs used for batching analytics): 180 days by default.

- Residency: If your tenant selects the EU region during onboarding, all hosted artifacts are stored in our EU data plane and do not cross into the US for storage or offline analytics. Cross-region replication is opt-in and requires an enterprise agreement.

- Deletion mechanisms and guarantees:
  1) Self-serve: Console retention policy page to set account-level windows (minimum 7 days, maximum 730 days).
  2) API: /v1/admin/data/purge to request a targeted purge for query IDs or date ranges. Purge jobs are asynchronous; we return a job id and completion timestamp.
  3) Manual escalation: Support can run an emergency purge for legal holds; this follows our documented playbook and is audited.

For forensic deletion: we delete primary objects from the storage layer and initiate background garbage collection for backups and caches. We provide an audit entry for every purge (job id, initiator, scope, timestamp). Note: immutable backups are retained for a bounded period only if you are on a Dedicated or Private plan where retention is customer-controlled — hosted backups are rotated per our backup retention SLA (default 35 days).

I'll loop in Neha for the PII/derivative artifact handling nuance — Michael, tagging you for any infra caveats. Attachment: retention_matrix_20271102.csv (high-level mapping). Also filing REDW-1234 to track follow-up doc for procurement.

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Wu <bethany.wu@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what does Redwood store by default (requests vs outputs) and how do we delete it?

Hi all — a couple of clarifications from the privacy team so your legal folks have exact language:

- "Prompts" vs "outputs": We classify anything submitted in the request body (user prompt, system messages, tool inputs) as "request artifacts." Model-produced sequences are "response artifacts." Both classes are subject to the retention windows Laura listed, but we treat customer-configured "diagnostics capture" specially: if a customer opts into diagnostics collection (used for quality and evals), we tag those records and they may be retained up to account-configured retention (max 730 days).

- PII/ESI: Customers can request targeted redaction/purge for specific user identifiers via the API purge endpoint. For hosted accounts, we do not automatically redact customer-provided text; we provide tooling and advice in the playbook. If your procurement requires automated PII redaction at ingestion, that's a Professional Services add-on.

- Audit evidence: We can supply an export of purge job audit entries (csv) and a statement of deletion (signed) for enterprise contracts.

If Acme wants an exact clause to paste into the MSA about default deletion timelines and EU residency, happy to draft a short paragraph.

-Neha
